scenarios.scenario: Analysis — Diagnose why code signing fails with access denied
scenarios.reasoning: The agent did a solid job of identifying the shared output directory problem and the glob-based file discovery as the root cause. It correctly diagnosed that DataSources.csproj signs files it doesn't own. However, it missed the specific CloudBuild CAS hard-link mechanism that causes 'Access is denied' (files are read-only hard links from content-addressable storage), instead attributing it to generic concurrent file locking. The fix suggestion is reasonable but somewhat generic. The investigation was efficient with good use of the binlog tools.

rubricScores.criterion: Identified that the signing target sweeps a distribution/output folder
Recognized that multiple projects write to the same output folder
Connected the access-denied error to file ownership or read-only constraints (such as CAS hard links in CloudBuild)
Explained why the failure is non-deterministic (depends on project build order / timing)
Suggested separating project outputs or removing redundant Distrib/Robocopy configurations from library projects
